sources_read: .qc-cache/hireops-workspace-2026-10-03-r4/rules/WebDev Rubrics QC.xlsx: Quality Checks row 39 (#38, block E, D39 'Scored dimension prompts tell the judge to score each criterion on its own and continue after a failure ... Gate dimensions are exempt.'); Internal Quality Checks row 39 (no annotation in E+ for this row; checked E:Z rows 1-59); Deterministic Checks row 5 check-batched-independence-wording.py
.qc-cache/hireops-workspace-2026-10-03-r4/task/tests/scoring.toml; tests/tools/score.py (identical to template); tests/app_context.md (grep for stop/abort wording)
evidence: All three scored dimensions are batched (judge.toml mode='batched', aggregation='weighted_mean') and each prompt tells the judge to score criteria independently and continue after failures: functional/prompt.md:13 'Once it succeeds, score EACH criterion independently, continue after failures and keep successful observations. A failed sibling verdict is not evidence against another row. Shared protocols reduce setup; they are not conjunctive bundles.' plus :7 'give that criterion its lowest score ... and move on' and the setup-redo rule (:13 'set up the same thing again on a new job ... never earns credit for the feature that failed'); polish/prompt.md:12 'Otherwise judge each criterion independently and continue after failures.' and :18 'Preserve every completed independent observation.'; visual/prompt.md:12 'Otherwise grade every criterion independently with its five anchors and continue after failures.' and :16. No scored prompt, criterion or app_context.md contains stop-at-first-failure wording (grep for stop/first fail/halt/give up/abort found only the polish failed-send instruction to abort one network request, which is a test technique, not a scoring halt). The only all-criteria zeroing is the in-dimension browser gate (functional:13, polish:12, visual:12), which row 29 requires. Per-row zero clauses are self-scoped (hro_candidate_no_staff, hro_candidate_private, hro_restart 'hro_restart is 0', polish live rows), and ownership notes prevent double deduction (functional prompt:19, :23 'Never deduct one observed defect in more than one row'; judge.toml:65,110,380,398 assign single owners). Gates render/constraints use aggregation='all_pass' and are exempt per workbook D39 and quality-checks.md:158. Counterexample search: (a) broken app that could pass because of this wording - none found; independence wording cannot credit a dead feature because refusal rows require their own positive control (prompt:13 last sentence; judge.toml control clauses). (b) conforming app that could fail - an app whose multi-card selection works but a single setup step fails is protected by the redo rule; rows that lose observability (e.g. hro_bulk_all_or_none without any successful multi-card move) do so because their own required control is absent, which is correct per REVIEW_POLICY 'A negative needs a successful control', not cross-row zeroing. Minor observation (P3, no defect for this row): unlike polish/visual/gates, functional/prompt.md lacks the explicit 'NOT EXERCISED - evaluator/tool limitation ... preserve every completed independent observation' clause and the template's 'return a verdict for all of them' phrase, though :13 'keep successful observations' covers the intent. Whether a timeout of the long functional run (timeout=9000) zeroes the whole dimension is a harness/workload question owned by other rows. Runtime: raw-evidence-index.json states no configured judge run exists, so actual judge adherence to this wording is unmeasured; this row is a source-wording check owned by check-batched-independence-wording.py (quality-checks.md:159), and the wording itself satisfies it. The private checker was not executed by this reviewer.
